images.title: Number names grow by tens
images.purpose: Shows that old Indian number names went up in powers of 10, each one 10 times the one before.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. A staircase of five steps rising from left to right, with a small arrow between each pair of steps.
images.exact_structure: Five flat rectangular steps of equal width, each one higher than the one on its left, filled teal (#0072B2) with dark outlines. On the face of each step, in white, its number, left to right: 1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000. Between each pair of neighbouring steps, one small curved amber (#E69F00) arrow rising to the next step, exactly 4 arrows, each labelled × 10. Above the top step, in grey (#6B7280): powers of 10. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Each old Indian number name was 10 times the one before, just like our numbers.
images.description: Shows that old Indian number names went up in powers of 10, each one 10 times the one before.
images.context: eka 1, dasha 10, shata 100, sahasra 1000, ayuta 10000; the names are said by the narrator, not drawn.

image_decisions.why: The idea that the names eka to ayuta climb by tens is clearest as a staircase of powers of 10.
